chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Kuleyb al-Asadi who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about al-Nabeez, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) addressed the people, so he (peace be upon him) said in his sermon: O people! Indeed, every intoxicant is prohibited. Indeed, and whatever a lot of it intoxicates, a little of it is prohibited.'

key_terms.النَّبِيذ: Al-Nabeez (a type of fermented drink made from raisins or dates)

ai.seo_question: What is the rule for consuming small amounts of a substance if a large amount causes intoxication?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the foundational Shia legal principle of 'kathiruhu haramun qaliluhu haram' (abundance makes it haram, scarcity makes it haram), specifically addressing the status of al-Nabeez, a pre-Islamic fermented drink. It underscores the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) comprehensive prohibition of all intoxicants, linking the physical effect of intoxication directly to the legal ruling of impurity and prohibition in Ja'fari fiqh.

en.hubeali: From him, from Muhammad Bin Abul Jaaabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Kuleyb Al Asady who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about Al-Nabeez, so heasws said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww addressed the people, so hesaww said in hissaww sermon: ‘O you people! Indeed! Every intoxicant is Prohibited. Indeed! And whatever, a lot of it were to intoxicate, so a little of it is Prohibited’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Kulayb al- Asadiy who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about al-Nabidh. He (the Imam) said that once the Messenger of Allah addressed the people and said, £ 0 people, all intoxicating liquor is unlawful. You must take notice that whatever in large quantity is intoxicating liquor, it in a small quantity also is unlawful.’”
